author: theoneric
body:
Since ASS rendering depends on the storage size of the video libass
needs to know about it to render the subtitles correctly. If it isn't
told about the storage size libass uses the value from PlayRes{X,Y} as
a guess, but this isn't always correct.
With Aegisub currently always rendering at storage resolution
this ends up the same as the frame size.

---

I'm confident the “rendering size == storage size” assumption holds true for Aegisub’s subtitle preview. From a glance it also appears to hold true for Aegisub’s csri frontends for CLI and AviSynth, but I'm less confident about those two. However, since csri currently only gets one size: if it isn't correct, this should also affect VSFilter-based backends.

You can see the different rendering on the following sample. Load it into Aegisub *without resampling to video resolution* and switch between xy-VSFilter or vsfilter_textsub *(**not** VSFilterMod!)* and libass; without the patch the result differs, with the patch it will match.

author: zloery
body:
This change adds a new step to the "create GCP context" flight to create a pet service account in the newly-created GCP project for the caller. Previously, pet SAs would only be created the first time they were explicitly requested from Sam. This is a small optimization to prevent the following failure case which has appeared a few times:

1. Sam immediately adds new pet SAs to the appropriate proxy group on creation. However, there can be a small delay (generally a few seconds) before GCP permissions granted to the proxy group apply to the new group member.
2. A common use of pet SAs in Workspace Manager is checking access to referenced cloud resources, which happens on referenced resource creation. If this is the first time a user's pet is needed in the workspace, WSM will request Sam create the pet SA and then immediately try to use the pet credentials.
3. WSM attempts to check permissions on a cloud resource using the pet SA. However, the SA was just created and GCP permissions have not propagated, leading to a false negative IAM check.

This is especially common while cloning workspaces, where WSM may attempt to read referenced resources from the source workspace immediately after creating the destination workspace.

body:
Signed-off-by: Anna Jung (VMware) <antheaj@vmware.com>

**Description of your changes:**
- Add Group and Version to ResourceAttributes needed for authorization
- Skip auth for an empty namespace

Fixes #7196, #6102

This bug allows users to upload pipelines by file but fails when trying to upload via URL. The difference I found between the two functions is that upload by file [skips authorization](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/0c0e4b61050e6fea6f20dd35e14eb3edc214bbba/backend/src/apiserver/server/pipeline_upload_server.go#L225) when the namespace is empty.

[With Pipeline UI currently not supporting namespace scoped creation](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/issues/4197#issuecomment-1042015539), it’s not possible for a user to authenticate against a specific namespace since the namespace passed to the request is always empty. 

To fix this bug, I remove the need for user authentication when uploading via URL by checking if the namespace is empty.

author: nhaghighat
body:
## Description

This PR changes the mounting structure to use PVC (persistance volume claims)
Helm charts creating the PVCs and then the orchest uses them. the names of the PVCs are hardcoded, so one of the next jobs should be to make it configurable.

If you want to test this PR with rook-ceph, the kvm have to be installed, after that minikube can be installed with following command:
`./scripts/install_minikube.sh -n 5`

If you want to test it with rook-nfs, there is no need for kvm. (the cluster with kvm also works)

Then you should install docker-registry with the following command in `deploy` directory:
`make docker-registry`
then the docker-registry port should be forwarded.
`export POD_NAME=$(kubectl get pods --namespace orchest -l "app=docker-registry,release=registry" -o jsonpath="{.items[0].metadata.name}")`
`kubectl -n orchest port-forward $POD_NAME 8080:5000`

then the new images can be built on the node(laptop), and tagged and pushed to our docker-registry:
`./scripts/build_container.sh -i celery-worker`
`docker tag orchest/celery-worker 127.0.0.1:8080/orchest/celery-worker`
`docker push 127.0.0.1:8080/orchest/celery-worker`

Then the value of `images.registry` of each chart you just pushed needs to be updated to the service ip of docker registry. 
finally you can start deploying the cluster with:

With rook-ceph:
` ENABLE_ROOK_CEPH=true make orchest`

With rook-nfs:
` ENABLE_ROOK_NFS=true make orchest`


## Checklist

- [x] The PR branch is set up to merge into `feat/k8s` instead of `dev`.
- [x] In case I changed code in the `orchest-sdk` I followed its [release
      checklist](https://github.com/orchest/orchest/blob/master/orchest-sdk/python/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md)
